result.notes:
Reference photo: a Toyota press photo of a 2020 GR Supra Launch Edition in Absolute Zero white. It is a real A90/MK5, confirmed by the lamps, fascia, badge and red mirror caps. The shot is straight-on at headlight height. The original was rolled 2.74 deg: the parking sensors differed by 24 px over 501 px. I levelled it with trace_tools rotate on the 3600 px original and cropped it to ref/front.jpg. The unlevelled crop is ref/front_raw.jpg. The candidate downloads are in ref/cand, including a second, higher-camera photo from the same shoot (az015) used to cross-check shapes.

A slight yaw remains: the viewer's right half shows more of the car's side. I traced the viewer's left half, whose inner features match the right side to within 2 px. Scale is 1 mm = 18.98 px, and the body is 80.5 x 37.46 mm (G80 is 38 mm tall).

Design decisions (G80 language):
- White = body paint: hood, round fender tops, the nose cone with the badge, the two fang pillars between the intakes, the body-colour blades under the outer intakes, and the lower corner legs.
- Black = the whole headlight lens, the side vents, both outer intakes, the central lower intake, one full-width splitter, the two parking-sensor rings and the badge. The splitter wraps up the outer corners as the canards and joins the central intake and the outer intakes' lower corners, as on the car.
- White on black = the light signature. The DRL is the lamp's outer and lower edge offset 1.0 mm into the lens, so the bezel outside it is exactly 0.65 mm. The three LED cells are 1.85 x 1.55 mm rounded squares along the lamp top, the same approach the AMG GT in this line uses for its LED cells.
- Relief = the line's honeycomb (built-in hex, pitch 2.4, rib 0.8) in all three intakes, because the real car has the same mesh in all of them. The outer intakes' upper inserts stay flat black at rib height. In the production build they read as a solid insert against the recessed mesh.
- Grooves (0.55 mm) = the hood's front shut line and the nose-cone crease. The crease leaves each lamp's inner corner and sweeps down under the badge. I compared full, short and no crease: the full version is the one that reads as the Supra's protruding centre nose.
- Sensor rings: r 0.95 mm, width 0.5, placed mid-pillar.

Printability: 0 design errors before repair and 0 auto-repairs. The remaining warnings are either by design (0.55 mm grooves, the badge's 0.5 mm strokes and cell tips) or cut honeycomb cells at the pocket walls, which the checker only warns about. I used 2 of the 3 full builds. In the first build the classic black part lost the two tiny black cells inside the badge's horizontal oval (area 0.54 mm2, coverage 0.55). I enlarged them to 0.83 mm2 and gave them rounded tips (r 0.12). In the second, final build all four slicecheck parts are ok, n_lost 0, top_layer_coverage 0.97 to 0.995, and a plate holds 13.

What I could not or did not do:
1. The brief mentions a tiny upper grille slot with the emblem. The real A90 nose (this photo and the higher-camera shot) is a solid painted nose cone with the badge, with no slot, so I drew none.
2. The badge is simplified to a black ellipse with the white vertical and horizontal ovals sharing their top. The chrome outer ring and the horizontal oval's lower arc inside the vertical oval are left out, because at 3.4 mm tall they can't be kept with gaps of at least 0.5 mm. The badge is about 7% larger than in the photo (7.0 x 3.44 mm vs 6.5 x 3.2 mm).
3. I made the lamp tail about 0.4 mm thicker than on the car so the DRL can run into it with a printable bezel.
4. The real mesh is horizontally stretched diamonds. I used the line's standard hex cell (points left and right) to keep the set consistent.
5. The narrow side vents (1.9 mm) are flat black with no mesh.
